title: The FanDuel and market-desk price records conflict
finding: The engine's Week 10 file contains 78 FanDuel-labelled records marked VERIFIED, all event=close and timestamped 2026-11-14T12:00:00Z; the market desk's Week 11 store has 39 empty MARKET_OPEN and 39 empty MARKET_CLOSE rows and says no operator quote was available. Engine archives match their recorded hashes, but they are short transcribed text summaries rather than original page-response bytes. The engine price-store docstring also says the store is empty-by-design, which does not match the committed CSV.
impact: Do not use these records to claim full open/close coverage, compute CLV/realized ROI, or clear a price-dependent gate until provenance, source/time/region, terms and scope are reconciled.
next_action: Owners of the engine and market desk should reconcile each record, explain what `close` and the common capture time mean, preserve permitted raw evidence, and align the store/documentation. Until then, leave price-dependent values blank and flagged.

title: R-13 says 32/32 rosters were captured; its cited sweep shows 1/32 populated

impact: Do not claim complete roster/reserve-list coverage or interpret a missing roster entry as availability. The cited NE roster link is only one club's source.
next_action: Market-desk owner: either supply row-level source/time/count evidence for all 32 clubs or amend the readiness statement within its scope; add a verifier that compares the claim to the populated roster rows.

title: Game Book references exist for 14 Week 10 games; extracted starter/inactive rows cover JAX–TEN only
finding: The Week 10 result CSV has 14 Game Book URLs. In the inspected namespace, the separate starter and inactive extractions have 44 and 12 rows, respectively, all for JAX–TEN. A separate nflverse (AGGREGATOR) 2026 snap-count file has 12,693 rows for 136 games and 32 clubs, but only REG weeks 1–9 (provenance date 2026-11-12); it is not direct Week 10/11 NFL Game Book coverage. The market desk's R-25 says 0 inactive and 0 snap-count rows in that desk's namespace, not repository-wide.
impact: Do not generalize one game's parsed lineup to all games or mark the market desk's own requirement met from another namespace. The third-party weeks 1–9 aggregate does not supply Week 10/11 coverage or substitute for per-game official extraction. Actual starters, inactives and current target-week snaps remain incomplete for a full-slate feature.
next_action: Record per-game source and extraction coverage, reconcile the namespace difference with both owners, and keep unobserved names/statuses blank. Do not infer depth from jersey number, experience or salary.

title: Different counts and correlation values are published from different capture windows
finding: The command desk holds 150 result rows and the market desk 145; their recorded update windows differ. Standings/correlation registers also cite 2026-11-14, 2026-11-15 and 2026-11-18 reads and produce different values. The date differences mean these are not demonstrated same-snapshot mismatches.
impact: Cross-desk comparisons can mix pre/post-result snapshots or different definitions. Do not combine the values or claim one is wrong until the inputs are aligned.
next_action: Pin one official standings/result snapshot with timestamp/hash, align club aliases, row universe and formulas, then recompute and publish n/uncertainty consistently.
